examples.target: How long have you been learning this language? You sound quite fluent.
Yes, I spent six months there, and my accent improved enormously.
What about vocabulary? I forget new words quickly.
I stopped being afraid of making mistakes and started speaking every day.
Did you do any kind of immersion, like living abroad?
No, but you need regular contact with a native speaker, in person or online.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: How long have you been learning this language? You sound quite fluent.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you! About three years, but I only became confident last year.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I stopped being afraid of making mistakes and started speaking every day.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: That is the hardest part for many learners, I think.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Definitely. Nobody learns to speak by only reading grammar rules.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Did you do any kind of immersion, like living abroad?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I spent six months there, and my accent improved enormously.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: Is it true that you must live in the country to learn a language well?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, but you need regular contact with a native speaker, in person or online.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: What about vocabulary? I forget new words quickly.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I do short reviews every day, and I use new words in real sentences.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: That makes sense. Do you ever feel that you are not improving?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Often. When that happens I change the method, for example by watching series without subtitles.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.text: I should try that. It sounds like fun.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It is, and it trains your ear. Be patient, and enjoy the process.
